plain_description.what: Re-judges 600 matches through the production Kotlin arena, now wired to the newer judge and prompt recipe. It compares the verdicts with the Python research scripts on identical inputs (1,200 calls).
plain_description.why: Every judged result since the new judge recipe came from Python scripts, so the production path had to be shown to give the same verdicts.
plain_description.information: A pass would allow mixing results from both paths. A fail means only a whole-board re-judge can be trusted. Result: done; FAIL as registered under one of the two tie-counting rules (-2.6 points, outside the 1.9-point bar). Under the other rule it was within the bar. Both paths sent identical bytes, so the gap is the provider's own randomness plus how ties are counted. A later whole-board re-judge found the two paths act as the same instrument within the judge's known noise floor.
